First release of `mkdocs-carve`: write MkDocs pages in
[Carve](https://markup-carve.github.io/carve/).

`.crv` files become documentation pages alongside your Markdown, rendered by the
Carve engine itself rather than by a Markdown extension approximating it.

```bash
pip install mkdocs-carve
```

```yaml
plugins:
  - carve
```

### What it does

- Claims `.crv` source files as MkDocs pages, with the rest of the MkDocs
  pipeline (navigation, theme, search) unchanged.
- Enables Carve extensions per site through the `extensions` config key,
  defaulting to `["heading_permalinks"]`. Ask the installed engine what it
  accepts: `python -c "import carve; print(carve.extensions())"`.

### Engine

Rendering is `carve-lang`, the PyO3 binding over carve-rs, so output matches the
Carve CLI for the same input.
